newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany agrees nationwide Scientology surveillance.
newsitem.headline: Germany agrees nationwide Scientology surveillance.

text.p: Interior ministers of Germany's 16 federal states said on Friday they had agreed to put the Church of Scientology under coordinated nationwide observation by the federal and state anti-extremist watchdogs.

The interior ministers, meeting for a two-day conference in Bonn, said they had decided that the group, which Germany sees as a profit-making organisation, not a religion, met the legal conditions necessary for observation.

"With Scientology there are really clues of efforts against the basic liberal-democratic order and therefore the legal prerequisite for an observation of the organisation by the protectorate of the constitution," the interior ministry of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern said in a statement.

The group has accused Germany of persecuting it and its members and of mounting an "hysterical witchhunt" against it at taxpayers' expense. Members said they planned to protest outside Chancellor Helmut Kohl's office later on Friday, when British Prime Minister Tony Blair was to arrive for talks.

Two large southern German states, Bavaria and Baden-Wuerttemberg, have already been carrying out surveillance on Scientology, which is based on the teachings of late American science fiction writer L. Ron Hubbard.

The states said the federal and state anti-extremist watchdogs would be asked to develop a joint working concept on how best to observe the group and present a report to the interior ministers' conference in a year.
The opposition Greens criticised the states' decision, calling the planned surveillance authoritarian.
"In contrast, a explanatory, civilised way of dealing with the Scientology organisation dominates in the rest of Europe," a group of Greens deputies said in a statement.
The Greens said problematic activities by the group should first be cleared up and criminal practices dealt with by the relevant legal authorities.
The German parliament's commission into "so-called sects and psycho-groups" is due to present its findings on the organisation to parliament on June 26.

This year's annual human rights report from the U.S. State Department listed Scientology's allegations of persecution in Germany, and the issue has prompted protests from U.S. entertainment celebrities.
